market.what: Hydrotreating catalyst used for diesel (ULSD) desulfurization, world
market.method: Hydrotreating catalysts $1.29-1.39B (3 reports) x ~40% diesel share (est.) = $0.53B; cross-check est. 28 mb/d gasoil x 365 x ~$0.05/bbl catalyst = $0.51B

value.logic: Sorbent pulls last 4,6-DMDBT (50->10 ppm) so HDS runs milder: ~1.9x less catalyst volume, est. ~30 scf/bbl less H2 (~$0.11/bbl at $1.5/kg) + catalyst ~$0.02/bbl = ~$0.13/bbl x 2.5 Gbbl/yr constrained units (25% of diesel, est.) = ~$0.3B. Must regenerate: 40 ppm S = ~5 g S/bbl
value.revenue_logic: Sorbent priced at ~30% of value ($0.1B if all adopt) x ~5% adoption by yr 7 = ~$5M; plus fuel-cell logistic-fuel niche
value.margin_logic: Specialty regenerable sorbent; organic receptor grafted on silica/resin, toll made

trend.drivers: Diesel demand flat to falling (EVs, LNG trucks); more sour/heavy crude and HVO co-processing keep HDS tight

direct_startups: SulfaTrap (2012, TDA spinout, sorbents for fuel-cell fuels)
competition.notes: Topsoe/Ketjen catalysts are the real rival: HDS keeps improving. Adsorptive ULSD at lab scale (CSIR-IIP/SINTEF). No funded diesel-polishing startup found

lab.synth: 1-2 step custom (bis-urea ammonium from isocyanate + polyamine) then graft on silica: s0 is insoluble in diesel, must be a solid sorbent
lab.test: Batch isotherms + breakthrough column with 4,6-DMDBT in dodecane and real ULSD feed; sulfur by ASTM D5453 UV fluorescence; 5 regen cycles; university lab
lab.logic: Synth+graft 3 variants 6-8 wk, $12-18k (CRO); tests 4 wk, ~$7k (~80 samples x $50-80)

sale.gates: Refinery slipstream pilot 6-12 mo; sorbent life and regen proof ~1 yr; partner licensor (Topsoe/Axens) or fuel-cell OEM
